newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel shells Lebanon village despite accord.
newsitem.headline: Israel shells Lebanon village despite accord.

text.p: Israeli gunners shelled a south Lebanese village, wounding 10 civilians in an escalation of its conflict with pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas, Lebanese security sources said on Saturday.
Israel said its artillery attack on Friday night was a direct reprisal for an attack by the Moslem guerrillas on its forces, although no one was hurt in the attack.

However, its action bypassed a monitoring mechanism set up last April under U.S. and French auspices which is designed to avert escalation of the conflict in south Lebanon and bans attacks from or at civilian areas.

The Israeli army later said in a statement that its troops killed two Amal guerrillas and wounded one in a clash in the Jewish state's occupied zone in south Lebanon on Friday. It did not say if it captured the wounded guerrilla.

Eight of the injured from the shelling of the village were from a single family and some were badly hurt when 13 155 mm heavy artillery shells hit the village of Safad al-Batikh, the Lebanese sources said. One man had a hand blown off and another lost a foot, they said.
Three houses were destroyed by direct hits and 37 other shells exploded close to the village, the sources added.

The attack was the most intensive shelling of a Lebanese village by Israel since a U.S.-brokered ceasefire understanding on April 26 ended a 17-day Israeli blitz of Lebanon intended to crush pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas.

The understanding included an undertaking by Israel and its South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia ally not to shell Lebanese civilians, stating that: "Israel and those cooperating with it will not fire any kind of weapon at civilians or civilian targets in Lebanon."
It said the two sides were committed to ensuring that "under no circumstances will civilians be the target of attack" nor would civilian areas be the launching ground for attacks.
However, the accord permitted Hizbollah the right to attack Israeli troops in the occupation zone and allowed Israel the right to self-defence.

The Israeli army said in a statement issued in Jerusalem that it shelled the village after Hizbollah guerrillas fired mortars from it at Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone which is manned by Israeli and SLA troops.
There were no casualties in the mortar attack, it said.
The army later amended its version of events after further investigation. It said the mortars were fired from the outskirts of Tavnin and Safad al-Batikh villages.
"The Israeli army wishes to emphasise that firing from near villages risks civilians," the later statement said.
An army spokesman said Israel would complain about the incident at a meeting of the monitoring committee on Monday.

Under the April 26 understanding a five-nation Monitoring Group, which meets at the headquarters of U.N. peacekeeping troops in the south Lebanon village of Naqoura, was set up to monitor application of the understandings.
